claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a closely matched derivative has room-temperature coercivity below or no greater than 100 Oe.
Approximately 650°C constitutes a sub-solidus annealing temperature for the proposed FeCoNi alloy or matched derivative.
Annealing FeCoNi at approximately 650°C for 2 hours will induce precipitation of a second phase.
The annealing treatment will produce dispersed nanoscale precipitates within an fcc matrix.
The precipitated second phase will be magnetically hard.
Rapid quenching after annealing will retain a primarily fcc matrix and avoid complete phase transformation.
The alloy is maintained as single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a single-phase fcc derivative during the treatment.
The precipitates will act as magnetic domain-wall pinning sites.
Domain-wall pinning by the precipitates will restrict domain-wall motion during magnetization reversal and thereby increase coercivity.
The specified annealing treatment will increase room-temperature coercivity beyond approximately 100 Oe.
The annealed material may exhibit at least a 50% increase in coercivity relative to the untreated matched baseline.
The coercivity increase will occur while high saturation magnetization is retained.
The hypothesis is restricted to fcc FeCoNi and similar high-entropy alloys treated at approximately 650°C for 2 hours in inert atmosphere followed by rapid quenching and measured at room temperature.
A coercivity increase of less than 50%, or failure to detect precipitates correlated with an enhancement, is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions say the treated alloy is maintained as single-phase fcc, whereas the hypothesis and structural mediator require precipitation of a distinct second phase. A primarily fcc matrix containing precipitates is multiphase, not single-phase.
